What's changing?" And in fact, it also says they seek diverse perspectives. (01:08:20): And that was a way of getting at what's called DEI, diversity, equity, and inclusion. That's a subtle nod towards if everyone in the room is a 50-year-old white man, you may not really be making the right overall decision for Amazon's customer base. You may be making the one for 50-year-old white suburban Seattleites. And so it's just some of these, every word in those has been studied as an individual word inside the company.
turns.zh: 那段内容被重新编辑了，特别注意历史修订的部分，真希望能看到编辑记录。原文被修改为"领导者会积极质疑自己的信念"。（01:07:58）关键在于要强调保持开放态度，时刻自问："是的，我认为自己是对的，但新证据在哪里？我学到了什么？情况有何变化？"实际上还提到要寻求多元视角。（01:08:20）这是在暗示DEI（多样性、公平性和包容性）理念。也就是说，如果会议室里全是50岁的白人男性，你可能无法为亚马逊的客户群做出正确决策，而只会为西雅图郊区的50岁白人男性服务。因此，公司内部对每个词汇都进行了细致研究。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Okay. Let's move on to the final area I wanted to spend a little time on, and this is called contrarian corner. I'm curious if you have any contrarian opinions about things basically that other people believe that you don't believe, something you see that many people don't see. Is there anything that comes to mind?
turns.zh: 太棒了。好的，接下来我想花点时间探讨最后一个话题，叫做"反向思考角"。我很好奇，你有没有一些与众不同的观点？比如别人都信奉的理论，你却不认同，或者你观察到许多人忽视的现象。能想到什么吗？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Yeah, I think a place where I'm currently very contrarian is the return to office movement. Many leaders at my level appear or publicly favor the need to get back into the office potentially full-time. (01:09:27): And I'm contrarian on this because of innovation. Specifically, I looked it up, you can check my facts on Wikipedia. The first purpose-built office, the first building ever built to be an office was built in 1726 in London. And so we're about 300 years into learning how to use offices well. (01:09:51): And what that means is offices aren't going to get much better. What's the last major thing you can think of that got better in offices? You might say well open offices, but a lot of people would say that's not even a good idea. These big rows of desks and loud pits. (01:10:06): With working from home, we've only been doing that for a few years since the pandemic began and at all since the internet started 20 years ago. Which one is likely to have more opportunity for improvement? There's so many things we haven't explored with remote work. And I think the people who say, "Back to the office, it's because we know it works," well we know what it is, but I have so much more faith in the opportunity to improve the remote experience. And so I think long-term, it's going to triumph. (01:10:40): The one other place where I'm a huge contrarian is doing business on a handshake. I understand companies need lawyers, and I have an attorney for certain things. But I coach people. Most of the people I coach, there's no NDA in place. There's no contract in place. They pay me through PayPal and I do good coaching for them. (01:11:01): I think too much of the world is contract driven, and we've lost the idea of your word being your bond, and you can actually trust me to follow through on my commitments. And I'm a contrarian there. (01:11:14): I realize I will occasionally get burnt. Someone will behave in a way, they'll let me down. But I think when we're always suspicious of people, that's a high cost. And the other place I'm contrarian is just doing business on faith.
turns.zh: 是啊，我认为我目前在一个非常逆向的领域，那就是重返办公室办公的潮流。许多我这个级别的领导人都公开表示或暗示，应该尽快全面重返办公室办公。（01:09:27）但我对此持反对态度，因为这关乎创新。具体来说，我查过资料，你可以在维基百科上核实。世界上第一座专门建造的办公楼，1726年就建在伦敦。也就是说，人类花了约300年的时间才逐渐掌握如何有效利用办公空间。（01:09:51）这意味着办公环境不会有太大改进了。你能想到最近办公环境有重大改进的地方吗？有人可能会说开放式办公室不错，但很多人认为这根本不是个好主意。那些排成一排的办公桌和喧闹的区域。（01:10:06）至于远程办公，自从疫情开始以来，才做了几年，而自从20年前互联网兴起以来，更是只有短短几年时间。相比之下，远程办公的改进空间要大得多。我认为那些说“必须回办公室上班”的人只是因为习惯了旧有模式。我们只知道现状，但我对改进远程办公体验更有信心。从长远来看，我认为远程办公会胜出。（01:10:40）另一个我非常反对的观点是靠握手交易做生意。我理解公司需要律师，但我自己也有律师处理某些事务。但我指导客户时，大多数情况下没有签署保密协议或合同。他们通过PayPal付款，我就为他们提供优质的指导服务。（01:11:01）我认为当今世界过度依赖合同条款，失去了"一诺千金"的传统理念，人们不再信任他人能履行承诺。这方面我持反对态度。（01:11:14）我知道偶尔会吃亏，有人会让你失望。但我认为如果总是怀疑别人，成本太高了。另一个我反对的观点就是凭信任做生意。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That reminds me, Sam Altman has a similar philosophy of just trust people and assume it'll all be okay. Sometimes you'll get burned, but on balance, it'll end up being much better for you and for everyone around you.
turns.zh: 这让我想起，山姆·奥尔特曼也有类似的理念，就是信任别人，相信一切都会顺利。有时你会吃亏，但总体来说，结果会对你和身边的人都更有利。

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: I didn't know that Sam had said that, but I strongly agree with it.
turns.zh: 我不知道山姆说过这话，但我非常认同。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, although he had some challenges recently. I don't know if it's working great, but it ended upgrade for him. So anyway, okay. We've actually reached our very exciting lightning round. Before we get there, is there anything else you wanted to touch on, or share, or leave listeners with?
turns.zh: 是啊，不过他最近遇到了一些挑战。我不知道现在情况是否理想，但对他来说总归是好事。所以好的，我们要进入激动人心的闪电问答环节了。在开始之前，你还有什么想补充、分享或留给听众的吗？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: No, I've really enjoyed this conversation. I could talk about careers forever and I love doing that, but I think we've covered a ton today that will really help people. So I'm good. Let's hit the lightning round.
turns.zh: 没有，我真的很享受这次对话。我可以永远聊职业发展，我也喜欢聊这个，但今天我们已经讲了很多对大家有帮助的内容。所以我很满意。开始闪电问答吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: All right. With that, we reached our very exciting lightning round. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 好的。现在就进入激动人心的闪电问答环节了。准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: I'm ready.
turns.zh: 准备好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Ethan, what are two or three books that you've recommended most to other people?
turns.zh: 伊桑，你向别人推荐得最多的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Two or three books. My number one recommendation is a book called Decisive. It's by Chip and Dan Heath, and it's about the science of making better decisions. The reason I recommend it so much is it will make your career better because leaders are decision makers, but also your personal life. So I apply it at least as much in my personal life as I do in my professional life. (01:12:47): My second most recommended book is Leadership and Self Deception, much less known than Decisive, a little bit harder to approach. It's by a group, a research group called the Arbinger Institute, and it's about, the self-deception is we cause a lot of our interpersonal problems while blaming them on others. And it walks through how are you part of the problem you're having with somebody else and what can you do about it? (01:13:14): The third and final book was recently brought to me by someone I work with that you know, Jason [inaudible 01:13:21]. That book is The Almanack Of Naval Ravikant. And Naval Ravikant is an angel investor responsible for AngelList. (01:13:30): But what I love about that book is he has a recipe. He really boils down how to be successful while loving what you do. And he says, "No one can be a better version of you." Don't try to copy me and be, "I'm going to be like Ethan, or I'm going to be like Lenny." Instead, figure out what you uniquely do best that you love, because no one can copy you being you. And that's your defensible sort of career value. And I really like that mental model.
turns.zh: 两三本书吧。我最推荐的一本是《决策的科学》（Decisive），作者是奇普和丹·希思。这本书讲的是如何做出更明智的决策。我之所以如此推荐它，是因为它能提升你的职业生涯——毕竟领导者就是决策者——同时也能改善你的个人生活。（01:12:47）我第二推荐的书是《领导力与自我欺骗》（Leadership and Self Deception），比起《决策的科学》名气小得多，理解起来也更困难。这本书由阿尔宾格研究所（Arbinger Institute）团队撰写，核心观点是——我们常常把人际关系问题归咎于他人，而实际上问题源于自身欺骗。这本书会教你如何认识到自己在人际关系中扮演的角色，以及如何改进。（01:13:14）第三本也是最近同事杰森（Jason）推荐给我的，那就是《纳瓦尔·拉维康特年鉴》（The Almanack Of Naval Ravikant）。纳瓦尔·拉维康特是天使投资人，也是AngelList的创始人。（01:13:30）我最喜欢这本书的地方在于，他提出了一个成功秘诀：热爱自己所做之事，同时保持专注。他说：“没有人能成为更好的你。”别试图模仿他人，比如“我想成为伊桑（Ethan）”或“我想成为莱尼（Lenny）”。相反，你应该找到自己独有的优势和热爱之事，因为没人能复制你的独特之处。这才是你不可替代的职业价值。我非常喜欢这种思维模式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, Naval has so many insightful messages, and you can read all these on his Twitter. We'll link to his Twitter, and someone just made a book out of his tweets basically. He's such an interesting dude.
turns.zh: 是啊，纳瓦尔有很多深刻的见解，你可以在他的推特上看到相关内容。我们会附上他的推特链接，甚至有人把他的推文集结成书了。他真是位有趣的人。

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Yes, that's right.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. What is a favorite recent movie or TV show you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 太棒了。你最近有没有特别喜欢的电影或电视剧？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: So I grew up on a farm, and so all the Taylor Sheridan, 1923, and Yellowstone, and all of those series, we've watched everything he's put out. We do kind of laugh like, wow. Are you familiar with Yellowstone at all?
turns.zh: 我从小在农场长大，所以泰勒·谢里丹（Taylor Sheridan）执导的《1923》和《黄石》等系列剧集，我们都看遍了。他拍的作品总能让人惊叹。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Absolutely. A lot of death.
turns.zh: 没错，里面经常有人死去。

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Yeah. At one point my wife and I were watching it, we would start betting. So the episode is starting, how many people will die in this episode? This ranch in Montana, but yet somehow they're always killing people. How does this work?
turns.zh: 是啊。我和妻子看剧时还会打赌。比如新一集开始时，我们会猜：“这一集会有几个人死去？”这部剧背景设在蒙大拿州的牧场，但不知为何总有人被杀。怎么回事呢？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's what your life was like, is what I'm hearing. Favorite interview question that you like to ask candidates?
turns.zh: 听起来你以前的生活也是这样。面试时你最喜欢问候选人的问题是什么？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: I think my favorite interview question is, "Tell me about a time where you needed to disagree with your management, where you needed to stand up or fight for a position against higher leadership or people in power." Because I think that's really hard to do. I'm normally interviewing leaders, and I think having a bunch of people who just say yes isn't helpful. You need people to have, as you said, have backbone, disagree and commit. So that's what I'm normally looking for.
turns.zh: 我最喜欢的面试问题是：“请讲讲你曾需要反驳上级、为自己的立场据理力争的经历。”因为这真的很难做到。我通常面试的是领导者，我觉得只会唯唯诺诺的人没什么用。你需要有骨气，敢于反驳，敢于坚持。这才是我真正看重的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Is there favorite product you've recently discovered that you really love?
turns.zh: 太棒了。最近有没有发现特别喜欢的产品？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: It's silly, but my favorite product that I've discovered recently is the Chuckit!, which you use to whip a ball for your dog a quarter mile. It basically extends your arm. And it's just fun to send a ball soaring way further than you could ever throw it. And you feel like, "Wow, look at me. I'm a major league pitcher." Because I have this three foot lever arm and I understand physics. If we look at tech products, there's so many I love. It's too easy to say ChatGPT and stuff, so I won't go there.
turns.zh: 这听起来有点傻，但我最近发现的最喜欢的产品是Chuckit！这款产品能帮你把球抛给狗狗，射程可达四分之一英里。这东西简直就像是把你的手臂延长了。看着球飞得比你自己能扔得远多了，那种感觉真是太棒了。你会忍不住感叹：“哇，看看我，我简直就是大联盟的投手！” 因为我拥有三英尺长的机械臂，而且我懂物理学。如果说到科技产品，我喜欢的实在太多了。说ChatGPT之类的大热门太容易了，所以我就不提了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. My dog does not love chasing balls, so I haven't had a reason to buy that, but I've never thought about just the joy of flicking a ball really far. Do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to, share with folks, find useful in work or in life?
turns.zh: 太棒了。我的狗狗不喜欢追着球跑，所以我还没机会买这个，但我从未想过把球抛得远远的能带来多大乐趣。你有没有最喜欢的的人生格言，经常回想、分享给别人，觉得对工作或生活很有用？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: I happen to be a Christian, and the motto that I think about the most is, "To whom much has been given, from him much will be required." And so I think a lot about what is my social responsibility. (01:16:44): I've been very lucky. I grew up on a farm in Ohio now. I wasn't a farm boy, my father was a chemist. But I grew up in upper middle class settings, and I've ended up being extremely successful, able to retire from my job at 50 to kind of coach and teach. What do I owe to pay forward? So those words are obviously ancient spiritual texts, but they're the ones I take away and think the most about. What's my responsibility?
turns.zh: 我恰好是基督徒，最常回想的格言是：“多给谁，就向谁多取。” 所以我经常思考自己的社会责任。（01:16:44）：我一直很幸运。我现在住在俄亥俄州的农场里，虽然我不是农场男孩，但父亲是化学家。我成长在中上阶层家庭，最终事业成功，50岁就能退休，开始指导和教学。我该如何回馈社会？这些古老的精神教诲显然对我影响深远，我经常思考自己的责任。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: As an example of someone that to whom much has been given, but because he's worked so hard, Jeff Bezos is starting a space business as you know. If you had the chance to go to space, would you go?
turns.zh: 以杰夫·贝索斯为例，他作为一个被赋予诸多资源的人，却通过努力开启了太空事业。如果有机会去太空，你会去吗？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Well, I of course saw his interview where he talked about how he thought about the safety and the conversation he had to have with his mother. I would like to go to space. I'm not willing to pay what I think the current tickets are, but I would take the risk. So what's the risk of that ride? One in a hundred, one in 50, even more that you won't come back. I would probably take the gamble.
turns.zh: 当然，我看过他接受采访，谈到如何考虑安全问题，以及和母亲的对话。我很想去太空。虽然我不愿支付目前的票价，但我愿意冒这个险。那么太空旅行的风险有多大？百分之一？五十分之一？甚至更大？不回来了？我大概会赌一把。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So you'd be an early adopter? Where along that curve would you be, an early adopter, laggard?
turns.zh: 那你会成为早期采用者吗？在创新曲线上，早期采用者还是落后者？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Well, I'm old enough that I remember when the Challenger space shuttle exploded, and I said I would get on the next one and I said, "They're never going to be more careful than the next one, so I'll get on the next one." (01:18:04): So I think I would get on any one I was offered because of the chance. Unlike Jeff who claims he wasn't scared, I would probably be really terrified, at least at liftoff. While you're up there, it's great. Everything either goes wrong going up or coming down. It's not the middle.
turns.zh: 嗯，我年纪够大，记得挑战者号航天飞机爆炸时，我说我会搭下一班航班，还说：“下一班肯定会更安全，所以我搭下一班。” （01:18:04）：所以只要有机会，我都会去尝试。和杰夫不同，他声称不害怕，我可能真的会很害怕，至少在升空时会如此。升空和返回阶段最容易出问题，而中间过程相对安全。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Ethan, I think we're going to help a lot of people with their career. I think we're going to help them work through failure, become better owners. Thank you so much for being here. Two final questions. Where can folks find you online if they want to reach out? Also, just share what you do now in case people could use that help. And then how can listeners useful to you?
turns.zh: 伊桑，我觉得我们能帮助很多人的职业生涯。帮助他们克服失败，成为更优秀的老板。非常感谢你今天的到来。最后两个问题。如果有人想联系你，网上哪里能找到你？还有，你现在做什么工作？或许能帮到其他听众？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: So the best place to find me online, I do all my writing on LinkedIn. It's where the professional community is. So Ethan Evans on LinkedIn. My actual handle there is Ethan Evans VP for my history as a vice president. That's the best place to find me. I do have a Substack newsletter. I do teach through the Maven platform, but all of those are linked off LinkedIn. (01:19:02): And really, how readers help me, they comment on what I write, because I miss things. I am one person's perspective. And so I actually have a process where I take in all the comments people write, all the different perspectives, all the different exceptions, or special cases, or examples, and that's how I improve my own thinking is I read every comment and think, "Okay, what did I miss? What could I have said better? How can I incorporate this if I ever talk about this again?"
turns.zh:
所以，要想在网上找到我，最好的地方就是领英。我所有的写作都在那里进行，那里汇聚了专业人士的社群。所以在领英上可以找到我，用户名是Ethan Evans。我的真实账号是Ethan Evans VP，源于我曾担任副总裁的经历。这是找到我的最佳途径。我确实有Substack订阅号，也通过Maven平台授课，但所有这些平台的链接都在领英上。

（01:19:02）：说真的，读者如何帮助我？他们会评论我的文章，因为我可能会忽略一些东西。我只是一个人的视角。因此，我有一个流程，会收集所有读者评论、不同观点、各种例外情况或特殊案例。通过这样，我能提升自己的思维水平——我会仔细阅读每条评论，思考：“我遗漏了什么？我本可以说得更好吗？如果我再谈论这个话题，该如何把这些观点整合进去？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just to give you another opportunity to plug the stuff you do now, what do you help people with in case people could value could you use the stuff that you offer? You said you coach, you have a course. What sort of stuff?
turns.zh: 再给你个机会宣传一下你现在做的事，如果有人能从中受益，你能利用你提供的服务吗？你提到你做教练，还有课程。具体是哪些方面？

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: I focus on two topics, career development. So how do you row in your career, the whole Magic Loop, and how do you attain promotion or attain a new role raise if that's your goal? And then leadership specifically. I teach a course that's been very popular called Stuck at Senior Manager - Breaking Through To Executive, which is how to get out of that sort of stuck, "I'm working really hard, I'm pretty good. I'm managing 25 or 50 people, but how do I get to the big chair? How do I get to the division level leadership and what do I need to change?" It's that whole what got you here won't get you there. And I love to see people succeed at that. People write me back and say, "I did get a job. I did get promoted, I did get a raise," and that's my fulfillment.
turns.zh: 我专注于两个主题：职业发展。比如如何在职业生涯中破局，整个“魔术循环”，以及如何获得晋升或新职位——如果这是你的目标。还有领导力方面。我教的一门非常受欢迎的课程叫《困在高级经理职位——突破到高管层》，它教人们如何突破停滞期。“我工作很努力，表现不错，管理着25或50个人，但如何登上高层宝座？如何进入部门级别领导层，我需要做出哪些改变？”这就是“过去的成功经验无法助你走向未来”这句话的具体体现。看到人们成功实现目标，比如获得晋升、加薪，我觉得特别有成就感。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Ethan, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 太棒了。Ethan，非常感谢你来参加节目。

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Thank you, Lenny. And I got to say, you are very good at this. You're so smooth and you just do a great job interviewing. It's been really been a pleasure.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，Lenny。不得不说，你做得非常出色。采访风格流畅自然，表现得很棒。真的很愉快。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I really appreciate that, and so are you. Thank you. Bye everyone.
turns.zh: 我很感激，你也是。谢谢。大家再见。

turns.speaker: Ethan Evans
turns.en: Bye everyone.
turns.zh: 再见。
